name: Nexabind
description: Nexabind is a neurotrophic growth factor cocktail that dramatically accelerates the integration of Synthetic Neural Tissue with organic nerve pathways, reducing standard SNT bonding time from 8–12 weeks to as little as 18 days. It works by upregulating axonal sprouting signals and suppressing the glial scar formation that normally slows SNT integration. Post-operative standard of care for any SNT implantation.
effects: enhanced myelin analog deposition around SNT threads
faster return to full augment functionality post-surgery
side_effects: vivid and disorienting sensory dreams during integration phase
temporary synesthetic cross-signaling between sensory channels
rare: runaway axonal growth causing unintended neural bridging between implant and nearby organic structures
emotional lability during the first week
cultural_context: Anyone who gets SNT implants needs Nexabind or its generic equivalents. The integration dreams it causes are notorious — users describe them as intensely real, often strange, and sometimes beautiful. On the Shelf, SNT surgery is rare and expensive, so Nexabind is mostly a Tier 2+ drug. Street surgeons use black-market Nexabind equivalents of dubious purity. Among augmentation enthusiasts in Tier 3, the 'binder dreams' are discussed almost reverently — some users microdose it recreationally for the synesthetic effects, which is medically inadvisable.
story_hooks: A black-market batch of Nexabind is causing the 'unintended neural bridging' side effect at a dramatically elevated rate — users are waking up with their SNT implants connected to emotional processing centers, making their chrome respond to feelings rather than intent.

A Helix Biosystems researcher has discovered that Nexabind's acceleration effect works on organic neurons too — in theory, it could be used to repair spinal cord damage, but the company has buried the finding because it would undercut their SNT product line.
A Tier 1 street surgeon is offering SNT work without Nexabind — clients are told they'll integrate naturally, but the process is going wrong and several are developing progressive motor dysfunction.
